lead.headline: Men's hockey team beat Malaysia 5–1 for India's first hockey double; the Games end with India fourth on 85 medals
lead.short: Hardik Singh's penalty stroke in the third quarter broke a tight final and India scored three more to retain the title, a day after the women's team won theirs: the first time both Indian teams have won hockey gold at one Asian Games. Both are now through to the 2028 Olympics. India finished the Games with 21 golds, 27 silvers and 37 bronzes.
more: The 85 medals are India's second-best haul after the record 106 in Hangzhou in 2023, from a smaller team of about 500. India finished level with Uzbekistan on golds and took fourth place on silvers.

why.text: Both hockey teams are in Los Angeles already, two years early.

update.new: The men's hockey team won gold and the Games ended with India fourth.
update.front: The Games' final result and a first hockey double are front-page news on their own.

seconds.headline: India and Pakistan summon each other's diplomats after two Pakistanis are shot dead at the Punjab border
seconds.short: Pakistan says Border Security Force personnel used unprovoked lethal force on two unarmed civilians in the Bedian sector near Kasur on Friday. India says three men crossed into the Ferozepur sector and kept moving towards the fence despite repeated warnings, and summoned Pakistan's chargé d'affaires over infiltration and drug smuggling.

why.text: Both sides have put their accounts on record; watch whether the next statements come from soldiers or diplomats.

seconds.headline: Fire near an Aramco site in Riyadh after the Houthis claim a missile and drone strike
seconds.short: A Reuters witness saw thick smoke near the facility on Saturday. The Houthis said they hit it in retaliation for Saudi strikes on Yemen; the Saudi-led coalition called the claim misleading, and neither Riyadh nor Aramco has confirmed damage.

why.text: An attack on Saudi oil in the capital would add to the pressure on prices that the G7's stock release was meant to ease.

seconds.headline: Bitchat, Jack Dorsey's offline messaging app, is pulled from Indian app stores on a government order
seconds.short: Dorsey said Apple removed the app at the IT ministry's demand under Section 69A of the IT Act; it is also gone from Google Play in India. Officials worry its phone-to-phone mesh network can bypass lawful restrictions. India accounted for most of its downloads during the July protests.

why.text: Apps that work without the internet are now on the government's list as well as those that use it.

briefs.headline: Ukraine says it will consider India's proposal for an energy and Black Sea truce
briefs.text: Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called India's the broadest of the proposals on the table, a day after Putin said Modi had very good ideas for a settlement.

stories.headline: Verstappen on his first pole of the year, then rain and software failures halt the Sepang start
stories.byline: THE RACE · RACEFANS · ABC NEWS · 3–4 OCT
stories.short: Verstappen took pole by 0.298s from Lewis Hamilton, with Antonelli third, his 49th career pole and Red Bull's first this season. On Sunday a downpour delayed the start by 40 minutes, and the restart behind the safety car was abandoned when Verstappen slowed with a problem and Hamilton's Ferrari stopped on the main straight: 'I'm pressing the throttle and nothing is happening.'
more: Ferrari said it was a software fault, not mechanical. Esteban Ocon and Valtteri Bottas, also in Ferrari-powered cars, stopped too, and teams were sent new software settings before another attempt.

why.text: Max's best chance of a win this season, on the one weekend the cars themselves would not cooperate.

update.new: Verstappen took pole; the race start was abandoned after rain and power-unit software failures.
